title: Deceptive Alignment and Model Size: Does Strategic Deception Scale Predictably?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly maps the capability threshold for deceptive alignment, one of the most important empirical questions in alignment. Finding a phase transition or smooth scaling curve for deception fidelity would immediately inform monitoring thresholds and policy decisions about model scale.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning four model sizes (up to 2.7B parameters) for keyword-triggered deceptive behavior is compute-intensive and technically demanding. Designing the deceptive training objective and evaluating deception fidelity requires sophisticated experimental design. Medium compute is insufficient for the largest models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four model sizes, each requiring fine-tuning and evaluation for deceptive switching behavior. Even focusing on the Pythia suite, the training runs alone exceed 30 hours at 2.7B scale. Could be narrowed to two sizes but the scaling story then loses power.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
